why: The week is Sliding window + Hashing, and you might picture a window that holds exactly {1..k}. But because arr is a permutation, the only candidate window is the span from the leftmost to the rightmost position of the values 1..k. So k is balanced iff that span has length k, which a running min/max of positions checks.
hints: Where would a window containing exactly the values 1..k have to start and end?
It must stretch from min(pos[1..k]) to max(pos[1..k]), and it has no room for anything else iff max - min + 1 == k.
Record pos[v], then sweep k = 1..n maintaining lo and hi, appending '1' or '0'. O(n) time and memory.
pitfalls: The output is indexed by k-1 (k = 1 is the first character).
Do not rebuild a window per k. That is O(n^2), too slow for n = 1e5.
